title: Who do buyers copy?
principle: People copy people like them. Show real, similar buyers.

screens.text: Let me tell you about some hotel towels. In an American hotel, scientists put a card in each bathroom asking guests to use their towels again. One card said: help save the environment. Another said: most guests at this hotel use their towels again.

screens.prompt: A third card said: most guests who stayed in this room used their towels again. Which card worked best?

options.label: Most guests who stayed in this room

screens.why: "This room" worked best. In one test, 35 of every 100 guests used towels again after the environment card, and 44 after "most guests at this hotel". In a second test, "guests who stayed in this room" got 49, the most of all.

screens.title: Social proof
screens.text: This is called social proof. When we're not sure what to do, we copy others, mostly people like us. "This room" felt closer than "this hotel". The more those people are like you, the more you want to copy them.

screens.title: It's used on you
screens.text: You see this every day: "bestseller" tags, star ratings, "1,200 bought this week". Some reviews are fake or paid for, and they mislead buyers. India's review standard, IS 19000, says bought reviews must not be published. So never fake reviews.

screens.title: Where it goes wrong
screens.text: Social proof can also make things worse. In an American national park, one sign said many past visitors had taken pieces of old wood that had turned to stone. The most wood went missing near that sign. It made taking wood seem normal.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Hotel guests and cake buyers think alike. It's early October. Your birthday-cake plan now serves 15 offices. The new colony has 120 homes, and 38 now order from you. Next is Lake View, with 300 flats nearby. Only 6 families there have ordered.

screens.prompt: The new colony has 120 homes, and many families already order from you. Which WhatsApp message will get the most new orders?

options.label: "38 families in this colony order from us"
"More than 500 happy customers across the city"
"The best eggless cakes in the city"

screens.why: Yes. Those 38 neighbours are people like them, and the number is real. "500 across the city" and "the best" say little about people like them.

wrong.b: "500 customers across the city" sounds big, but buyers don't know who those people are. 38 real neighbours in their own colony are more likely to make them order.
wrong.c: Every baker can say "the best". It tells buyers nothing about who orders from you. 38 real neighbours in their colony mean more to them.

screens.prompt: 6 of the 15 offices on your birthday-cake plan haven't paid this month. Which message will make them most likely to pay?

options.label: "Many offices pay late. Please pay soon"
"9 of our 15 offices have already paid"
"Why haven't you paid yet? Please pay now"

screens.why: Exactly. It shows that most offices have paid, so the ones who haven't paid may want to do the same.

wrong.a: That's like the national park sign. "Many pay late" makes paying late seem normal. Instead, show that most offices have paid: "9 of our 15 have already paid".
wrong.c: An angry message may upset people, and you could lose an office. Instead, show that most offices have paid: "9 of our 15 have already paid".

screens.prompt: I'll show you six ways to show social proof. For each one, tell me: is it honest, or does it mislead?

items.text: A customer's party photo, shared with her permission
Ask your cousin to post a 5-star review
"38 families in this colony order from us", a true count
A real buyer's voice note, shared with her permission

screens.why: Honest proof comes from real buyers who agree to share it. Reviews from family, paid reviews and hiding bad reviews all mislead buyers.

screens.setup: It's mid-October. You now deliver to Lake View every day. The 6 families there who ordered liked your cakes. 38 families in the new colony order often. Each cake leaves you ₹450.
screens.question: What do you post in the Lake View group?

options.label: "38 happy families!" with their photos and permission
options.outcome: It's true, but Lake View families don't know those people. 4 new families order in a month, leaving you ₹1,800.
options.why: Real proof helped, but it came from people they didn't know. People are more likely to copy their neighbours.
options.better: Show your 6 Lake View buyers, with their permission.

options.label: "Lake View's favourite!" with reviews from relatives
options.outcome: 2 families order. Then someone sees that a review came from your cousin. She tells the group, and the admin removes your post. You earn ₹900 and lose trust.
options.why: Fake proof may work until someone finds out. Then you can lose more than you gained.
options.better: Show your 6 Lake View buyers, with their permission.

options.label: "6 Lake View families ordered!" with their permission
options.outcome: Two of the six share photos of their cakes. Their neighbours ask questions. 10 new families order in a month, leaving you ₹4,500.
options.why: 6 real neighbours worked better than 38 people from another colony. The number is small, but buyers are more likely to copy people who live near them.

screens.title: The honest line
screens.text: The line again: use on others only what you'd accept being used on you. Show real buyers, with their permission. Never buy or fake reviews, or hide bad ones. You wouldn't want to buy from a shop that did this.
People copy people ___ them, so show ___ buyers.
screens.why: Exactly. "Guests who stayed in this room" worked better than "save the environment". Your 6 Lake View neighbours worked better than 38 people from another colony. Real buyers who are like your buyers are the best proof.

summary: Social proof: when we're unsure, we copy others, mostly people like us.
Show real, exact numbers from nearby buyers: "38 families in this colony" works better than "thousands love us".
Never make wrong actions seem normal. Never buy or fake reviews, or hide bad ones.

cards.front: Which message brings more orders in a colony?
options: "38 families in your colony order from us"
cards.back: People copy others like them. Real numbers from nearby buyers work best.

cards.front: Some clients pay late. Which reminder works best?
options: "Many clients pay late, but please pay"
"Most of our clients have already paid"
cards.back: Don't make paying late seem normal. Show that most clients have already paid.

cards.front: Your cousin offers to post a 5-star review. Should you let her?
cards.back: Fake or paid reviews mislead buyers, and India's review standard says bought reviews must not be published.

sources.label: Goldstein, Cialdini and Griskevicius, A Room with a Viewpoint (2008), figures as reported in the PLoS ONE replication (2014)
Cialdini et al., Managing social norms for persuasive impact (Social Influence, 2006): the Petrified Forest signs
